assignments.title: Practical 1 — Write to Solve a Problem: Recognising Online Scams in Nigeria
assignments.description:
Before You Click That Link: How to Recognise and Avoid Online Scams in Nigeria.

Your task is to research and write a professional educational article that helps young Nigerians recognise online scams and protect themselves from digital fraud.

Imagine you have been commissioned by a digital awareness organisation to create an educational article for young people, students, freelancers and small business owners.

Many people receive suspicious messages, encounter fake online stores, fall for fraudulent investment opportunities or unknowingly share sensitive information with scammers.

The problem is that some people do not know how to identify these warning signs until they have already lost money or compromised their personal information.

Your job is to help change that.
assignments.instructions:
RESEARCH FIRST

Do not write based solely on what you already know. Use at least three credible sources, including official consumer-protection or financial-awareness resources.

You can begin with:

1. Central Bank of Nigeria — Fraud and Scam Awareness
   https://www.cbn.gov.ng/supervision/cpdfraudandscam.html

2. Global Anti-Scam Alliance — State of Scams Nigeria 2026

3. Other credible sources, including relevant Nigerian regulatory agencies and reputable cybersecurity organisations.

Verify any statistics, claims or recommendations before including them. Do not invent statistics or present assumptions as facts.

YOUR TASK

Research the subject thoroughly and write an informative, engaging and practical article that answers the following questions:

1. What are some common forms of online scams people encounter in Nigeria?
2. How do scammers manipulate people's emotions, trust and urgency?
3. What are the warning signs that an online offer, message or transaction may be fraudulent?
4. How can someone verify whether a business, website, investment opportunity or message is legitimate?
5. What should someone do if they suspect they have been scammed?
6. What practical habits can people develop to protect themselves online?

WRITING REQUIREMENTS

- Format: Professional educational article.
- Length: 800-1,200 words.
- Audience: Young Nigerians, students, freelancers and small business owners.
- Tone: Professional, informative, conversational and authoritative.
- Headline: Create an attention-grabbing headline that communicates the value of the article.
- Introduction: Begin with a compelling opening that makes the reader recognise the problem.
- Body: Organise your ideas into clear sections with descriptive subheadings.
- Examples: Use realistic examples to explain how scams happen.
- Solutions: Give practical steps readers can apply immediately.
- Conclusion: End with a strong takeaway that reinforces the importance of digital awareness.

SUBMISSION

Submit your completed article as a document or PDF in the intranet.

Include your sources at the end of the article.
assignments.requirements:
WHAT YOU WILL BE GRADED ON

1. RESEARCH — Are at least three credible sources used, and are claims actually supported by them?

2. ACCURACY — Are the facts, statistics and recommendations correct and properly attributed? Nothing invented.

3. COVERAGE — Does the article answer all six questions in the brief?

4. STRUCTURE — Is there a strong headline, an opening that frames the problem, clear subheadings, and a conclusion that lands?

5. PRACTICAL VALUE — Could a reader act on this immediately to protect themselves?

6. WRITING — Is it clear, organised and readable at 800-1,200 words, with a professional and authoritative tone?

7. SUBMISSION — Is the article submitted as a document or PDF, with sources listed at the end?

Don't just write to fill a page. Write to make a difference.

assignments.title: Practical 2 — The Writer's Editing Room
assignments.description:
Theme: Good writing is not just about what you say. It is about how effectively you say it.

A professional content writer must be able to do more than produce original content. They must also recognise weak writing, identify what is missing, and transform an average piece into something worth reading.

For this practical, you have been given a LinkedIn-style article that needs improvement. Your job is to edit it, restructure it, and make it significantly stronger.

The original article is not terrible. In fact, an average reader might consider it perfectly acceptable. Your job is to recognise why acceptable writing is not necessarily excellent writing.
assignments.instructions:
THE ORIGINAL WRITE-UP

Title: Why You Need to Start Taking Your Personal Growth Seriously

Personal growth is one of the most important things that everybody needs to focus on in their life. In the world we live in today, things are changing very fast and if you are not growing, then you are probably staying in one place while everybody else is moving forward.

I remember when I used to think that I had everything figured out. I had goals, I had plans and I was always telling myself that I was going to become a better version of myself. But somehow, I kept finding myself in the same position every time.

The truth is that growth is very important because it helps you become better in every area of your life. Whether it is your career, your relationships, your finances or your mindset, you need to constantly work on yourself if you want to achieve success.

One thing I have realised is that you cannot expect your life to change if you keep doing the same things every day. You have to be intentional about your growth. You have to read books, listen to podcasts, learn new skills and surround yourself with people who are going somewhere in life.

Another thing is consistency. A lot of people want to become successful, but they don't want to put in the work. They want results immediately, and when things don't happen as quickly as they expected, they give up. But growth takes time, and you need to understand that.

There are different ways to improve yourself. You can start by waking up early, setting goals, planning your day, learning something new and making sure that you are always doing something productive. Even if you are only improving by one percent every day, it will eventually make a big difference.

You should also stop comparing yourself to other people because everybody has their own journey. Some people are ahead of you, while some people are behind you. What matters is that you keep moving forward and never allow anything to stop you.

At the end of the day, personal growth is a journey and not a destination. You have to keep learning, keep improving and keep becoming better because the person you become tomorrow depends on what you do today.

So start taking your growth seriously. Your future self will thank you for it.

What are you doing today to become a better person? Let me know in the comments.

YOUR TASK

You are the editor responsible for improving this piece before it is published.

Read the article carefully. Do not assume that because the writing is grammatically correct, it is already good writing.

Identify weaknesses in areas such as:

- The headline and opening hook.
- The strength and originality of the central message.
- Repetition and unnecessary statements.
- The flow and organisation of ideas.
- The use of examples and personal storytelling.
- The depth and usefulness of the advice.
- The connection between the writer and the reader.
- The conclusion and call to action.

PART ONE: EDITORIAL REVIEW

Before rewriting, identify at least five weaknesses in the original article. Explain briefly:

1. What the problem is.
2. Why it weakens the article.
3. What you intend to do differently.

PART TWO: REWRITE

Rewrite the entire article. Your revised version should:

- Have a stronger and more interesting headline.
- Open with a hook that makes readers want to continue.
- Communicate one clear central message.
- Remove unnecessary repetition.
- Have a natural and engaging flow.
- Use specific examples rather than relying entirely on generic advice.
- Sound human, intelligent and relatable.
- Give readers something practical to think about or apply.
- End with a meaningful conclusion and a relevant call to action.

You are allowed to change the structure, introduce a better angle and completely rewrite sentences where necessary. However, retain the central theme of personal growth.

PART THREE: PUBLICATION

Once you have completed your rewrite, prepare it for publication. Publish your improved article on LinkedIn or another appropriate social media platform.

Take a screenshot of your published article and submit it alongside your editorial review and rewritten version.

SUBMISSION

1. Your editorial review.
2. Your improved article.
3. Screenshot of the published article.

Make the difference between the original and your revised version obvious.
assignments.requirements:
WHAT YOU WILL BE GRADED ON

1. EDITORIAL REVIEW — Did you identify at least five genuine weaknesses, each with the problem, why it weakens the piece, and what you will do differently?

2. DIAGNOSIS — Are the weaknesses real, or just cosmetic? Did you spot repetition, weak opening, generic advice and structural problems?

3. REWRITE QUALITY — Is the revised article genuinely stronger: a better hook, one clear message, no padding, specific examples?

4. ORIGINALITY — Does it sound like a person with a perspective, or a reworded version of the original?

5. THEME RETAINED — Is personal growth still the subject, however much the angle changed?

6. PUBLICATION — Is the improved article published, with a screenshot submitted?

7. SUBMISSION — Are all three parts present: review, rewrite and screenshot?

We want to see your ability to think like an editor, not just write like an author.
